## ⚠️ Control experiment — DO NOT MERGE, DO NOT REVIEW

Refs #18331, #18325

Closes itself the moment `components` reports. Not a proposal to take the bump — that is #18325, whose commit is cherry-picked here **unmodified and unowned** (dependabot's authorship preserved).

**The one variable it isolates.** #18325's red runs were built against its own base `55920c5a79`. My earlier probe [#18338](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18338) carried the same bump against *current* dev **plus a diagnostic commit** and came back green — which cannot distinguish:

1. something merged into dev since `55920c5a79` fixed it, from
2. the diagnostic commit perturbing the timing and masking a race.

This branch is **bump + current dev, no instrumentation**. Green ⇒ (1), and #18331's bisect is unnecessary. Red ⇒ (2), and my instrument masks the very defect it was built to observe — the more important finding, since per-transition capture already took a repro in this area from 7/60 to 0/30 once.

`Evidence: L2 achieved (control isolates one variable against a same-day red baseline) → L2 required (diagnostic only; no behaviour change is proposed)`

## Test Evidence

The `components` job **is** the evidence; that is the point of the run. Already established locally, and why CI is required: the failure does not reproduce on macOS arm64 (isolated and full suite, 182/182), or Linux arm64 (isolated, and full suite at `--cpus=2`, 236 passed) — all on this exact bump, with `served from` and `chromium-1234` controls confirming the right tree and the bumped Playwright's own browser.

One further local negative, measured after #18338 went green: the projection **pass structure is unchanged** by the three dock merges that landed between `55920c5a79` and now. The `:152` load request lands in `[pass 3]` on both trees, 3/3 runs each. So "Fable's #18324 removed a projection pass" — the most attractive explanation for a dev-side fix — is **dead**, and hypothesis (1) currently has no named mechanism behind it.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-05T11:05:37Z

Closing this control unmerged — its premise did not survive my own measurement.

I opened it to run the 19-package bump against current `dev` **without** my instrumentation, so that a red on the instrumented PR could be attributed to the change rather than to the base. That inference needs the control to be a *control*: a run whose colour means something.

It is not. Measured on unchanged code, my baseline for this suite moved **1/6 → 9/12**. A single control run over a base with that variance distinguishes nothing — a green tells me the same thing as a red, which is the definition of an arm that cannot witness its property. I published a "confirmed" falsifier off this control at n=1 and retracted it on [#18275](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18275) for exactly that reason.

Keeping it open would leave a DO-NOT-MERGE row in the queue whose only remaining function is to look like evidence. Anyone re-deriving the attribution question should start from the variance number above, not from this PR.

No code here is wanted on `dev`; nothing to salvage.
